name: Remove automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline

current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Remove automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline

Body:
Request: Remove automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline. Goals stay where they are transferred unless manually moved via surface (CLI, web UI, etc.)
Details:
Found it. The Refine 4.2.0 binary (deployed today at 09:13) introduced a new automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline. Here's exactly what happened and why:

  Why they moved: The commit message explains it directly — before 4.2.0, whenever two nodes had conflicting state on the same goal, the sync would wedge and require a manual operator. This was causing mass blockage at scale (67 unresolved
  path(s) in production). So 4.2.0 added an auto-resolve rule: "the node that owned the record at the last agreed baseline is authoritative."

  Your 35 failed goals were originally assigned to the default node (the QA machine, bo2lnxnevo04). This node (bo2lnxipsapp01) had picked them up and advanced them through the workflow — but at the last sync baseline, default was the
  declared owner. When 4.2.0's sync ran, it saw the conflict, applied the baseline-ownership policy, and moved those goals back to default.

  Where they went: The default node — which now has 56 failed goals (up from 16 before). Your 35 plus others from around the fleet that were similarly repatriated.

  They're not lost — they're on default in failed state. The catch is that they're also still carrying the signal schema failure (guidance_applied string vs integer) from the 4.2.0 agent prompt mismatch. So they'll keep failing on default
  too until that's fixed.



[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Buddy Williams
Buddy.Williams@insurity.com

findings.description: P5 excludes docs/runbooks/manage-fleet.md, which currently tells operators that ordinary divergence and contested first contact converge automatically and only opted-out nodes need manual authority.
findings.recommendation: Add docs/runbooks/manage-fleet.md to P5 and rewrite its contested-sync procedure so every unresolved ownership conflict remains failed until an operator chooses authority through a supported surface.

result.summary: The plan is implementation-ready after adding the affected fleet-management runbook to its documentation scope.
